sources.claim: Multiple target tracking policies for a scalable target must use different metrics.
Multiple target tracking policies for an ECS service must use different metrics; managed alarms are removed when policies are deleted.
PutScalingPolicy creates or updates policies; deregistering a target deletes its policies.

safety.network: Owned VPC/subnet only; no internet gateway, NAT, or public IPv4 created.

findings.rule: A second predefined CPU policy is rejected even with a different target value.
findings.message: Only one TargetTrackingScaling policy for a given metric specification is allowed.

findings.rule: Exact custom metric duplication and dimension-order-only changes are rejected.
Updating an existing policy into another policy's predefined or custom metric is rejected without modifying either policies or managed alarm configurations.

Standard and high-resolution CPU specifications coexist after high-resolution monitoring deployment completes; managed CPU alarms retain distinct 60-second and 20-second periods. Another high-resolution CPU specification is rejected.

Without fully enabled high-resolution monitoring, high-resolution writes fail on that prerequisite rather than establish metric uniqueness. Earlier calls are retained, not interpreted as duplicate rejections.
findings.message: High-resolution metrics are not fully enabled on the ECS service.

findings.rule: Changing the custom metric Statistic from Average to Sum creates a distinct allowed specification for the otherwise identical metric.
Omitted Unit and explicit None are the same custom specification for uniqueness.
An identical metric-math specification is rejected.

failedWriteAtomicity.comparison: Complete described policy objects; all managed-alarm fields except dynamic State* fields. Lists sorted by policy or alarm name. Every raw before/after response remains in calls.

zeroTasksEvidence.basis: All three services were created with desiredCount=0 and targets min=max=0. No RunTask or StartTask call, no metric publication, no positive desired count, no public networking. Final RUNNING, PENDING and STOPPED task lists were empty in every owned cluster; service and cluster counters were zero.

additionalPrimarySources.claim: High-resolution CPU and memory metric types require 20-second monitoring; updates require successful deployment completion.
Custom specifications expose metric dimensions, statistic, unit and metric-math queries.

uncertainties: Metric-math equivalence under renamed query identifiers, reordered query lists, omitted ReturnData, equivalent expressions or reordered nested dimensions was not probed.
Other statistic and unit pairs, custom-versus-predefined equivalence, and ResourceLabel equivalence were not probed.
Task definitions were deregistered and verified INACTIVE, not permanently deleted.
runInterpretation: Three bounded sequential owned stacks; calls 1-74 initial ownership and atomicity, 75-136 monitoring-update prerequisite observations, 137-216 completed-monitoring ownership plus statistic/unit/metric-math boundaries. Every stack's cleanup is recorded in runs. Top-level prefix/resources/cleanup describe the final run.
